## R. PDP SPONSOR REIMBURSEMENT TO PHARMACIES [42 CFR §§ 423.505(b)(21) and 423.520]

1. If a PDP Sponsor uses a standard for reimbursement of pharmacies based on the cost of a drug, PDP Sponsor will update such standard not less frequently than once every 7 days, beginning with an initial update on January 1 of each year, to accurately reflect the market price of the drug.
2. If the source for any prescription drug pricing standard is not publicly available, PDP

Sponsor will disclose all individual drug prices to be updated to the applicable pharmacies in advance for their use for the reimbursement of claims.

3. PDP Sponsor will issue, mail, or otherwise transmit payment with respect to all claims submitted by pharmacies (other than pharmacies that dispense drugs by mail order only, or are located in, or contract with, a long-term care facility) within 14 days of receipt of an electronically submitted claim or within 30 days of receipt of a claim submitted otherwise.
4. PDP Sponsor must ensure that a pharmacy located in, or having a contract with, a longterm care facility will have not less than 30 days (but not more than 90 days) to submit claims to PDP Sponsor for reimbursement.

## Article III Record Retention and Reporting Requirements

## A. RECORD MAINTENANCE AND ACCESS

PDP Sponsor agrees to maintain records and provide access in accordance with 42 CFR §§ 423.505(b)(10) and 423.505(i)(2).

## B. GENERAL REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

PDP Sponsor agrees to submit information to CMS according to 42 CFR §§ 423.505(f) and 423.514, and applicable Final Medicare Part D Reporting Guidance.

## C. CMS LICENSE FOR USE OF PLAN FORMULARY

PDP Sponsor agrees to submit to CMS each plan's formulary information, including any changes to its formularies, and hereby grants to the Government, and any person or entity who might receive the formulary from the Government, a non-exclusive license to use all or any portion of the formulary for any purpose related to the administration of the Part D program, including without limitation publicly distributing, displaying, publishing, or reconfiguration of the information in any medium, including www.medicare.gov, and by any electronic, print, or other means of distribution.

## Article IV HIPAA Provisions

- A. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the confidentiality and enrollee record accuracy requirements specified in 42 CFR § 423.136.
- B. PDP Sponsor agrees to enter into a business associate agreement with the entity with which CMS has contracted to track Medicare beneficiaries' true out-of- pocket costs.

Article V

## Requirements of Other Laws and Regulations

PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with (a) applicable Federal laws and regulations designed to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse, including, but not limited to, applicable provisions of Federal criminal law, the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729 et seq.), and the anti-kickback provision of § 1128B of the Act; (b) applicable Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) rules at 45 CFR Parts 160, 162, and 164; and (c) all other applicable Federal statutes and regulations.

## Article VI Contract Term and Renewal

## A. TERM OF CONTRACT

This contract is effective from the date of CMS's authorized representative's signature through December 31, 2025. This contract shall be renewable for successive one-year periods thereafter according to 42 CFR § 423.506.

## B. QUALIFICATION TO RENEW A CONTRACT

1. In accordance with 42 CFR § 423.507, PDP Sponsor will be determined qualified to renew its contract annually only if PDP Sponsor has not provided CMS with a notice of intention not to renew in accordance with Article VII of this contract.
2. Although PDP Sponsor may be determined qualified to renew its contract under this Article, if PDP Sponsor and CMS cannot reach agreement on the bid under Subpart F of 42 CFR Part 423 and CMS declines to accept the bid pursuant to 42 CFR § 423.265(b)(4), no renewal takes place, and, in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.502(d)(2), the failure to reach agreement is not subject to the appeals provisions in Subpart N of 42 CFR Part 423.

45|CMS|The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is the federal agency responsible for administering the Medicare Part D Prescription Drug Benefit program in the United States. As the primary oversight body, CMS manages the entire lifecycle of Medicare Part D Prescription Drug Plans (PDPs), from initial contract approvals to ongoing compliance monitoring and enforcement. CMS contracts with PDP Sponsors to deliver prescription drug coverage to Medicare beneficiaries, ensuring that these sponsors meet federal regulatory standards and contractual obligations. The agency plays a central role in evaluating and approving PDP Sponsor bids, which are critical to determining which plans will be offered in each region. Additionally, CMS is responsible for setting the regulatory framework that governs the operation of PDPs, including requirements related to formulary design, pricing, network adequacy, and beneficiary access to medications. Throughout the program’s implementation, CMS oversees compliance with federal laws and regulations, conducting audits and reviews to ensure that PDP Sponsors adhere to established standards. The agency also manages contract modifications and, when necessary, initiates contract terminations to protect the integrity of the program and the interests of beneficiaries. By maintaining rigorous oversight and enforcement mechanisms, CMS ensures that the Medicare Part D program operates efficiently, transparently, and in alignment with federal policy objectives. 10|MEDICARE PART D MANUFACTURER DISCOUNT PROGRAM FINAL GUIDANCE|The Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance is a comprehensive regulatory document issued by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to implement the manufacturer discount requirements established under § 1860D-14C of the Social Security Act. This final guidance outlines the specific procedures and criteria that pharmaceutical manufacturers must follow to provide required discounts to Medicare Part D plans. The primary objective of the program is to ensure that beneficiaries enrolled in Medicare Part D receive cost-saving benefits through reduced drug prices, thereby lowering their out-of-pocket expenses. 

The guidance details how manufacturers must calculate and report discounts based on the average manufacturer price (AMP) and the best price (BP) of covered outpatient drugs. It specifies the timing, methodology, and documentation required for manufacturers to comply with the discount obligations, ensuring transparency and consistency across the program. By mandating these discounts, the program aims to improve the affordability of prescription drugs for Medicare beneficiaries while also aligning with broader federal efforts to control healthcare costs.

CMS emphasizes that the final guidance is designed to be enforceable and to support the integrity of the Medicare Part D program. It provides clarity on how manufacturers should report discount data to CMS, how these discounts are applied to Part D plan payments, and how the savings are ultimately passed through to beneficiaries in the form of lower premiums, reduced cost-sharing, or improved plan benefits. The guidance also addresses potential compliance issues and outlines the consequences for non-compliance, reinforcing the importance of adherence to the statutory requirements.

Overall, the Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance serves as a critical tool in shaping the financial and operational framework of drug pricing within the Medicare Part D program. It ensures that pharmaceutical manufacturers contribute to the sustainability of the program by providing meaningful discounts, which in turn helps reduce the financial burden on Medicare beneficiaries. This structured payment approach helps beneficiaries budget more effectively and ensures continued access to prescription drugs without the need for large, one-time payments. 46|PDP SPONSOR|PDP SPONSOR refers to a private organization or entity contracted with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to offer Medicare Part D Prescription Drug Plans (PDPs) to eligible Medicare beneficiaries. As a key participant in the Medicare Part D program, a PDP SPONSOR is responsible for administering prescription drug benefits, managing formularies, collecting premiums from beneficiaries, and ensuring compliance with federal regulations, including those established under the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act (ARRA) and other relevant statutes. These sponsors operate under specific CMS contract terms and are accountable for overseeing drug utilization, coordinating with pharmacies for reimbursement, and maintaining operational standards to ensure the delivery of quality, cost-effective prescription drug coverage.

Each PDP SPONSOR operates within a defined geographic region, providing coverage to beneficiaries in that area. The organization must maintain rigorous compliance with federal regulatory requirements, including those related to plan design, data reporting, beneficiary protections, and financial accountability. As a health plan organization, the PDP SPONSOR plays a central role in managing the entire lifecycle of the prescription drug benefit, from plan development and enrollment to claims processing and member services.

The responsibilities of a PDP SPONSOR extend beyond administrative functions; they include the development and maintenance of a formulary that balances cost, safety, and efficacy, as well as the implementation of utilization management strategies such as prior authorization, step therapy, and quantity limits. Additionally, PDP SPONSORS must ensure timely and accurate reimbursement to retail and mail-order pharmacies, while also providing beneficiaries with clear information about coverage, costs, and available medications.

In summary, a PDP SPONSOR is a private, CMS-contracted entity that administers Medicare Part D prescription drug benefits, ensuring that Medicare beneficiaries receive access to necessary medications in accordance with federal regulations and contractual obligations. Their role is critical to the effective operation of the Medicare Part D program, combining regulatory compliance, financial management, and beneficiary service delivery across a defined service area.|105

0|Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and Medicare Part D Community|"# Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and Medicare Part D Community

The community centers on the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) as the central regulatory and administrative authority overseeing the Medicare Part D Prescription Drug Plan program. Key entities include Prescription Drug Plan Sponsors (PDP Sponsors), who operate under formal contracts with CMS, and a network of regulatory, guidance, and operational documents that govern program implementation. The community is structured around a cyclical contract process, with the 2025 Solicitation for Applications released on January 9, 2024, serving as a pivotal event for contract renewals and program redesign. CMS maintains oversight through compliance mechanisms, including the C & D Data Group, which manages Part D data and reporting, and ensures adherence via regulations, guidance documents, and training. The community’s integrity depends on the interplay between federal law, regulatory frameworks, and operational execution by PDP Sponsors.

## CMS as the central regulatory authority

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) serves as the primary governing body for the Medicare Part D program, exercising comprehensive authority over its administration, regulation, and oversight. As a U.S. federal agency within the Department of Health and Human Services, CMS is responsible for administering Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP, with a central role in managing Medicare Part D, including the Voluntary Prescription Drug Plan (PDP) program. CMS establishes the legal and operational framework through federal laws such as the Social Security Act and regulations like 42 CFR Part 423, which define eligibility, benefits, enrollment, and sponsor responsibilities. The agency ensures compliance across state and private sector partners by setting payment rates, monitoring performance, and enforcing standards. Its role extends to driving innovation in health care delivery and payment models, reinforcing its foundational position in the U.S. health care system [Data: Entities (0), Relationships (0, 6, 36, 79, 73, 76, 306, +more)].

## Prescription Drug Plan Sponsors operate under CMS contracts

Prescription Drug Plan Sponsors (PDP Sponsors) are private entities authorized by CMS to operate Medicare Part D plans, providing prescription drug benefits to eligible beneficiaries. These sponsors enter into formal contracts with CMS, which govern their operations, compliance obligations, and financial responsibilities. The contract relationship is central to the community’s structure, with CMS overseeing sponsor activities, approving plan designs, and ensuring adherence to federal rules. PDP Sponsors must meet eligibility criteria outlined in 42 CFR § 423.503 to be approved and are protected from new, significant regulatory requirements during the contract term, except at the beginning of a calendar year or when mandated by statute. This contractual framework ensures continuity and stability in plan operations while allowing CMS to enforce compliance through audits, reporting, and data monitoring [Data: Entities (1), Relationships (0, 16, 17, 22, 40, +more)].

## Regulatory and guidance framework ensures program compliance

The Medicare Part D program operates under a robust regulatory and guidance framework established by CMS and codified in federal law. The Social Security Act provides the legal foundation for Part D, while 42 CFR Part 423 implements the program through detailed regulations covering eligibility, benefits, enrollment, and sponsor responsibilities. Specific regulations such as 42 CFR § 423.100 define the basic and supplemental benefits that must be offered, and 42 CFR § 423.516 protects sponsors from mid-contract regulatory changes. CMS issues a suite of guidance documents—including the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, Participant Guides, and Communications and Marketing Guidelines—to ensure consistent interpretation and application of rules. These documents are critical for PDP Sponsors to understand their obligations and for CMS to maintain program integrity. The regulatory environment is further reinforced by the Health Plan Management System Memos, which provide internal procedural updates for operational implementation [Data: Entities (2, 3, 7, 8, 12, 13, 15, 18, 20, 21, 22, 307, +more); Relationships (36, 40, 71, 72, 76, 82, 85, +more)].

## The 2025 Solicitation and contract renewal cycle drives program continuity

The 2025 Solicitation for Applications for Medicare Prescription Drug Plan Contracts, released on January 9, 2024, marks a critical milestone in the program’s annual cycle. This formal solicitation outlines the requirements and procedures for entities to apply for or renew contracts to operate Part D plans for the 2025 contract year. It serves as the primary mechanism for maintaining continuity with the prior contract year (2024), which is being renewed under the current contract document. The solicitation enables CMS to evaluate new and existing sponsors, set terms, and align program design with federal policy objectives. The renewal process ensures that PDP Sponsors can continue providing benefits while incorporating updates from the Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, which govern changes to plan design and beneficiary coverage. This cyclical process reflects CMS’s structured approach to program management and long-term planning [Data: Entities (4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11, 15, 21, 22, 307, +more); Relationships (5, 58, 69, 70, +more)].

## C & D Data Group manages compliance and data integrity

The C & D Data Group, a division within CMS, plays a vital role in managing data related to Medicare Part D drug benefits and compliance reporting. This group is responsible for ensuring the accuracy, consistency, and integrity of data used to monitor plan performance, assess compliance, and support program evaluation. Vanessa S. Duran, the Director of the C & D Data Group, is authorized to sign contracts on behalf of CMS, underscoring the group’s strategic importance. The C & D Data Group supports CMS’s oversight function by collecting, analyzing, and disseminating data on drug pricing, beneficiary enrollment, premium collection, and manufacturer discount reporting. This data is essential for enforcing regulatory requirements, identifying compliance risks, and informing policy decisions. The group’s work is integral to the transparency and accountability of the Part D program [Data: Entities (159, 151, 307); Relationships (306, 307, +more)].

## Manufacturer discount and payment plan programs enhance beneficiary affordability

Two key CMS initiatives—the Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance and the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance—directly impact beneficiary affordability and program sustainability. The Manufacturer Discount Program requires pharmaceutical manufacturers to provide discounts on covered outpatient drugs based on average manufacturer price (AMP) and best price (BP), with the savings passed through to beneficiaries via lower premiums, reduced cost-sharing, or improved benefits. The Final Guidance provides detailed procedures for calculating, reporting, and applying these discounts, ensuring compliance and transparency. Simultaneously, the Prescription Payment Plan allows beneficiaries to pay their Part D premiums in installments, reducing financial burden and improving access. These programs reflect CMS’s commitment to controlling healthcare costs and improving access to affordable prescription medications for Medicare beneficiaries [Data: Entities (10, 11, 15, 21, 22, 307, +more); Relationships (71, 72, +more)].

## Training and communication ensure consistent program implementation

CMS conducts regular training sessions and provides communication materials to ensure that PDP Sponsors and other stakeholders understand and comply with Part D rules and contract obligations. These trainings are designed to clarify complex regulatory requirements, operational procedures, and compliance expectations, reducing the risk of errors and non-compliance. The Health Plan Management System Memos serve as internal communications to guide the implementation of new regulations and procedural updates. Additionally, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines regulate how PDP Sponsors may market their plans to beneficiaries, ensuring transparency, accuracy, and ethical practices. These efforts collectively promote consistency, accountability, and public trust in the Medicare Part D program [Data: Entities (15, 8, 13, 12, 15, 21, 22, 307, +more); Relationships (14, 76, 73, +more)]."

0|CENTERS FOR MEDICARE & MEDICAID SERVICES|The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is a U.S. federal agency within the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) responsible for administering key federal health programs, including Medicare, Medicaid, and the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP). As a central regulatory and operational body, CMS ensures the effective delivery of health care services to millions of Americans by overseeing program compliance with federal laws and regulations. The agency plays a critical role in managing Medicare, which provides health insurance to individuals aged 65 and older, as well as certain younger people with disabilities. This includes the administration of Medicare Part D, the Medicare Prescription Drug Plan, which helps beneficiaries access affordable prescription medications. CMS is responsible for establishing the rules and standards for this program, negotiating with and overseeing contracts with Prescription Drug Plan Sponsors, and ensuring that these plans meet federal quality and coverage requirements. In addition to its role in Medicare, CMS administers Medicaid, a joint federal and state program that provides health coverage to low-income individuals and families, and CHIP, which extends health insurance to children in families with incomes too high to qualify for Medicaid but too low to afford private insurance. Through its regulatory authority, CMS sets payment rates, establishes eligibility criteria, monitors program performance, and enforces compliance across state and private sector partners. The agency also drives innovation in health care delivery and payment models, aiming to improve quality, reduce costs, and expand access to care. Overall, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services serves as a cornerstone of the U.S. health care system, ensuring that federal health programs operate efficiently, equitably, and in accordance with national policy objectives.|19

0|## CONTRACT WITH APPROVED ENTITY PURSUANT TO SECTIONS 1860D-1 THROUGH 1860D-43 OF THE SOCIAL SECURITY ACT FOR THE OPERATION OF A VOLUNTARY MEDICARE PRESCRIPTION DRUG PLAN

## CONTRACT (<<CONTRACT\_ID>>)

Between

Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (hereinafter referred to as 'CMS')

And

## <<CONTRACT\_NAME>>

(a Prescription Drug Plan Sponsor, hereinafter referred to as 'PDP Sponsor')

CMS and PDP Sponsor, an entity that has been determined eligible to operate a Voluntary Medicare Prescription Drug Plan by the Administrator of CMS under 42 CFR § 423.503, agree to the following for the purposes of §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31) of the Social Security Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').

## Article I

## Voluntary Medicare Prescription Drug Plan

- A. PDP Sponsor agrees to operate one or more Medicare Voluntary Prescription Drug Plans (hereinafter referred to as a 'PDP'), as described in its application and related materials submitted to CMS for Medicare approval, including but not limited to all the attestations contained therein, and in compliance with the provisions of this contract, which incorporates in its entirety the 2025 Solicitation for Applications for Medicare Prescription Drug Plan Contracts, released on January 9, 2024 (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'the contract'). PDP Sponsor also agrees to operate in accordance with §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31) of the Act, the regulations at 42 CFR Part 423 (with the exception of Subparts Q, R, and S), and the solicitation, as well as all other applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies outlined in guidance, such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance, Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance, CMS Participant Guides, Health Plan Management System memos, Rate Announcement, and trainings. Except as provided in paragraph (C) of this Article, this contract is deemed to incorporate any changes that are required by statute to be implemented during the term of this contract and any regulations implementing or interpreting such statutory provisions.
- B. CMS agrees to perform its obligations to PDP Sponsor consistent with §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 of the Act (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31), the regulations at 42 CFR Part 423 (with the exception of Subparts Q, R, and S), and the solicitation, as well as all other applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies outlined in guidance, such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance, Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance, CMS Participant Guides, Health Plan Management System memos, Rate Announcement, and trainings.
- C. CMS agrees that it will not implement, other than at the beginning of a calendar year, regulations under 42 CFR Part 423 that impose new, significant regulatory requirements on PDP Sponsor. This provision does not apply to new requirements mandated by statute. [42 CFR § 423.516]
- D. If PDP Sponsor had a contract with CMS for Contract Year 2024 under the contract ID number designated above, this document is considered a renewal of the existing contract. While the terms of this document supersede the terms of the 2024 contract, the parties' execution of this contract does not extinguish or interrupt any pending obligations or actions that may have arisen under the 2024 or prior year contracts.
- E. This contract is in no way intended to supersede or modify 42 CFR Part 423. Failure to reference a regulatory requirement in this contract does not affect the applicability of such requirements to PDP Sponsor and CMS.

## A. ENROLLMENT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to accept new enrollments, make enrollments effective, process voluntary disenrollments, and limit involuntary disenrollments, as described in 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart B.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the prohibition in 42 CFR § 423.104(b) on discrimination in beneficiary enrollment.
3. PDP Sponsor shall accept enrollment applications from individuals who change their election during the open enrollment period for individuals enrolled in Medicare Advantage described in 42 CFR § 422.62(a)(3), as required by 42 CFR § 423.38(e).

## B. PRESCRIPTION DRUG BENEFIT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide the basic prescription drug coverage as defined under 42 CFR § 423.100 and, to the extent applicable, supplemental benefits as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100 and in accordance with Subpart C of 42 CFR Part 423. PDP Sponsor also agrees to provide Part D benefits as described in PDP Sponsor's bid(s) approved each year by CMS (as referenced in the Medicare Advantage Attestation of Benefit Plan, which is included in the contracting materials, and to be replaced each year upon renewal of the contract to reflect PDP Sponsor's approved bids for the succeeding contract year).
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to calculate and collect beneficiary premiums in accordance with 42 CFR §§ 423.286 and 423.293. PDP Sponsor also agrees to

## Article II

## Functions to be Performed by PDP Sponsor

1860D-2 of the Social Security Act for 2025, and Response to Relevant Comments and Medicare Prescription Payment Plan: Final Part Two Guidance on Select Topics, Implementation of Section 1860D-2 of the Social Security Act for 2025, and Response to Relevant Comments.

## C. DISSEMINATION OF PLAN INFORMATION

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide the information required in 42 CFR § 423.48.
2. PDP Sponsor acknowledges that CMS releases to the public the following data, consistent with 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart K:
3. (a) Summary reconciled Part D payment data after the reconciliation of Part D payments, as provided in 42 CFR § 423.505(o)(1); and
4. (b) Part D Medical Loss Ratio data for the contract year, as described at 42 CFR § 423.2490.
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to disclose information to beneficiaries in the manner and the form specified by CMS under 42 CFR § 423.128 and 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart V.

## D. QUALITY ASSURANCE/UTILIZATION MANAGEMENT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to operate quality assurance, drug utilization management, drug management, and medication therapy management programs, and to support electronic prescribing, in accordance with Subpart D of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to address and resolve complaints received by CMS against the PDP Sponsor through the CMS complaint tracking system as required in 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(22).
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to maintain a Part D summary plan rating score of at least 3 stars as required by 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(26).
4. PDP Sponsor agrees to pass an essential operations test prior to the start of the benefit year. This provision only applies to new sponsors that have not previously entered into a Part D contract with CMS and neither it, nor another subsidiary of the applicant's parent organization, is offering Part D benefits during the current year. [42 CFR § 423.505(b)(27)]

## E. APPEALS AND GRIEVANCES

PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with all requirements in Subpart M of 42 CFR Part 423 governing coverage determinations, grievances and appeals, and formulary exceptions, and the applicable provisions of Subpart U.

## F. PAYMENT TO PDP SPONSOR

1. PDP Sponsor and CMS agree that payment under this contract is governed by the rules in Subpart G of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with all applicable Federal laws and regulations, guidance, and authorities pertaining to claims and debt collections. In the event that the Government determines that PDP Sponsor has been overpaid, PDP Sponsor agrees to return those overpaid monies back to the Government.

## G. BID SUBMISSION AND REVIEW

If PDP Sponsor intends to participate in the Part D program for the next program year, PDP Sponsor agrees to submit the next year's bid, including all required information on premiums, benefits, and cost-sharing, by the applicable due date, as provided in Subpart F of 42 CFR Part 423 so that CMS and the PDP Sponsor may conduct negotiations regarding the terms and conditions of the proposed bid and benefit plan renewal.

## H. STATE LAW AND LICENSURE REQUIREMENTS

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with State law to the extent that it is not preempted by Federal law as described in Subpart I of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees that where it is operating in a State using a waiver granted pursuant to 42 CFR § 423.410, such waiver shall be valid for three consecutive program years. PDP Sponsor agrees that expiration of the licensure waiver (and the failure to obtain a license from the relevant State) may be the basis for CMS deleting from PDP Sponsor's service area those PDP Regions affected by the waiver expiration. CMS may terminate or non-renew PDP Sponsor's contract where the expiration of the waiver results in PDP Sponsor not being qualified to offer a PDP plan in any PDP Region.

## P. CERTIFICATION OF DATA THAT DETERMINE PAYMENT

PDP Sponsor must provide certifications in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(k).

## Q. ENROLLMENT RELATED COSTS

PDP Sponsor agrees to payment of fees established by CMS for cost sharing of enrollment related costs in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.6.

## R. PDP SPONSOR REIMBURSEMENT TO PHARMACIES [42 CFR §§ 423.505(b)(21) and 423.520]

1. If a PDP Sponsor uses a standard for reimbursement of pharmacies based on the cost of a drug, PDP Sponsor will update such standard not less frequently than once every 7 days, beginning with an initial update on January 1 of each year, to accurately reflect the market price of the drug.
2. If the source for any prescription drug pricing standard is not publicly available, PDP

Sponsor will disclose all individual drug prices to be updated to the applicable pharmacies in advance for their use for the reimbursement of claims.

3. PDP Sponsor will issue, mail, or otherwise transmit payment with respect to all claims submitted by pharmacies (other than pharmacies that dispense drugs by mail order only, or are located in, or contract with, a long-term care facility) within 14 days of receipt of an electronically submitted claim or within 30 days of receipt of a claim submitted otherwise.
4. PDP Sponsor must ensure that a pharmacy located in, or having a contract with, a longterm care facility will have not less than 30 days (but not more than 90 days) to submit claims to PDP Sponsor for reimbursement.

## Article III Record Retention and Reporting Requirements

## A. RECORD MAINTENANCE AND ACCESS

PDP Sponsor agrees to maintain records and provide access in accordance with 42 CFR §§ 423.505(b)(10) and 423.505(i)(2).

## B. GENERAL REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

PDP Sponsor agrees to submit information to CMS according to 42 CFR §§ 423.505(f) and 423.514, and applicable Final Medicare Part D Reporting Guidance.

## C. CMS LICENSE FOR USE OF PLAN FORMULARY

PDP Sponsor agrees to submit to CMS each plan's formulary information, including any changes to its formularies, and hereby grants to the Government, and any person or entity who might receive the formulary from the Government, a non-exclusive license to use all or any portion of the formulary for any purpose related to the administration of the Part D program, including without limitation publicly distributing, displaying, publishing, or reconfiguration of the information in any medium, including www.medicare.gov, and by any electronic, print, or other means of distribution.

## Article IV HIPAA Provisions

- A. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the confidentiality and enrollee record accuracy requirements specified in 42 CFR § 423.136.
- B. PDP Sponsor agrees to enter into a business associate agreement with the entity with which CMS has contracted to track Medicare beneficiaries' true out-of- pocket costs.

Article V

## Requirements of Other Laws and Regulations

PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with (a) applicable Federal laws and regulations designed to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse, including, but not limited to, applicable provisions of Federal criminal law, the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729 et seq.), and the anti-kickback provision of § 1128B of the Act; (b) applicable Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) rules at 45 CFR Parts 160, 162, and 164; and (c) all other applicable Federal statutes and regulations.

## Article VI Contract Term and Renewal

## A. TERM OF CONTRACT

This contract is effective from the date of CMS's authorized representative's signature through December 31, 2025. This contract shall be renewable for successive one-year periods thereafter according to 42 CFR § 423.506.

## B. QUALIFICATION TO RENEW A CONTRACT

1. In accordance with 42 CFR § 423.507, PDP Sponsor will be determined qualified to renew its contract annually only if PDP Sponsor has not provided CMS with a notice of intention not to renew in accordance with Article VII of this contract.
2. Although PDP Sponsor may be determined qualified to renew its contract under this Article, if PDP Sponsor and CMS cannot reach agreement on the bid under Subpart F of 42 CFR Part 423 and CMS declines to accept the bid pursuant to 42 CFR § 423.265(b)(4), no renewal takes place, and, in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.502(d)(2), the failure to reach agreement is not subject to the appeals provisions in Subpart N of 42 CFR Part 423.

## F. PAYMENT TO PDP SPONSOR

1. PDP Sponsor and CMS agree that payment under this contract is governed by the rules in Subpart G of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with all applicable Federal laws and regulations, guidance, and authorities pertaining to claims and debt collections. In the event that the Government determines that PDP Sponsor has been overpaid, PDP Sponsor agrees to return those overpaid monies back to the Government.

## G. BID SUBMISSION AND REVIEW

If PDP Sponsor intends to participate in the Part D program for the next program year, PDP Sponsor agrees to submit the next year's bid, including all required information on premiums, benefits, and cost-sharing, by the applicable due date, as provided in Subpart F of 42 CFR Part 423 so that CMS and the PDP Sponsor may conduct negotiations regarding the terms and conditions of the proposed bid and benefit plan renewal.

## H. STATE LAW AND LICENSURE REQUIREMENTS

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with State law to the extent that it is not preempted by Federal law as described in Subpart I of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees that where it is operating in a State using a waiver granted pursuant to 42 CFR § 423.410, such waiver shall be valid for three consecutive program years. PDP Sponsor agrees that expiration of the licensure waiver (and the failure to obtain a license from the relevant State) may be the basis for CMS deleting from PDP Sponsor's service area those PDP Regions affected by the waiver expiration. CMS may terminate or non-renew PDP Sponsor's contract where the expiration of the waiver results in PDP Sponsor not being qualified to offer a PDP plan in any PDP Region.

3. As set forth in 42 CFR § 423.508, if the contract is modified by mutual consent, PDP Sponsor must notify its Medicare enrollees of any changes that CMS determines are appropriate for notification according to the process and timeframes specified by CMS.
4. If a contract is terminated under this section, PDP Sponsor must ensure the timely transfer of any data or files.

A PDP Sponsor that agrees to terminate its offering of PBPs in a PDP region also agrees that it will not be eligible to apply to resume offering plans in that region for 2 years. 0|## CONTRACT WITH APPROVED ENTITY PURSUANT TO SECTIONS 1860D-1 THROUGH 1860D-43 OF THE SOCIAL SECURITY ACT FOR THE OPERATION OF A VOLUNTARY MEDICARE PRESCRIPTION DRUG PLAN

## CONTRACT (<<CONTRACT\_ID>>)

Between

Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (hereinafter referred to as 'CMS')

And

## <<CONTRACT\_NAME>>

(a Prescription Drug Plan Sponsor, hereinafter referred to as 'PDP Sponsor')

CMS and PDP Sponsor, an entity that has been determined eligible to operate a Voluntary Medicare Prescription Drug Plan by the Administrator of CMS under 42 CFR § 423.503, agree to the following for the purposes of §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31) of the Social Security Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').

## Article I

## Voluntary Medicare Prescription Drug Plan

- A. PDP Sponsor agrees to operate one or more Medicare Voluntary Prescription Drug Plans (hereinafter referred to as a 'PDP'), as described in its application and related materials submitted to CMS for Medicare approval, including but not limited to all the attestations contained therein, and in compliance with the provisions of this contract, which incorporates in its entirety the 2025 Solicitation for Applications for Medicare Prescription Drug Plan Contracts, released on January 9, 2024 (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'the contract'). PDP Sponsor also agrees to operate in accordance with §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31) of the Act, the regulations at 42 CFR Part 423 (with the exception of Subparts Q, R, and S), and the solicitation, as well as all other applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies outlined in guidance, such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance, Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance, CMS Participant Guides, Health Plan Management System memos, Rate Announcement, and trainings. Except as provided in paragraph (C) of this Article, this contract is deemed to incorporate any changes that are required by statute to be implemented during the term of this contract and any regulations implementing or interpreting such statutory provisions.
- B. CMS agrees to perform its obligations to PDP Sponsor consistent with §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 of the Act (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31), the regulations at 42 CFR Part 423 (with the exception of Subparts Q, R, and S), and the solicitation, as well as all other applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies outlined in guidance, such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance, Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance, CMS Participant Guides, Health Plan Management System memos, Rate Announcement, and trainings.
- C. CMS agrees that it will not implement, other than at the beginning of a calendar year, regulations under 42 CFR Part 423 that impose new, significant regulatory requirements on PDP Sponsor. This provision does not apply to new requirements mandated by statute. [42 CFR § 423.516]
- D. If PDP Sponsor had a contract with CMS for Contract Year 2024 under the contract ID number designated above, this document is considered a renewal of the existing contract. While the terms of this document supersede the terms of the 2024 contract, the parties' execution of this contract does not extinguish or interrupt any pending obligations or actions that may have arisen under the 2024 or prior year contracts.
- E. This contract is in no way intended to supersede or modify 42 CFR Part 423. Failure to reference a regulatory requirement in this contract does not affect the applicability of such requirements to PDP Sponsor and CMS.

## A. ENROLLMENT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to accept new enrollments, make enrollments effective, process voluntary disenrollments, and limit involuntary disenrollments, as described in 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart B.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the prohibition in 42 CFR § 423.104(b) on discrimination in beneficiary enrollment.
3. PDP Sponsor shall accept enrollment applications from individuals who change their election during the open enrollment period for individuals enrolled in Medicare Advantage described in 42 CFR § 422.62(a)(3), as required by 42 CFR § 423.38(e).

## CONTRACT (<<CONTRACT\_ID>>)

Between

Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (hereinafter referred to as 'CMS')

And

## <<CONTRACT\_NAME>>

(a Prescription Drug Plan Sponsor, hereinafter referred to as 'PDP Sponsor')

CMS and PDP Sponsor, an entity that has been determined eligible to operate a Voluntary Medicare Prescription Drug Plan by the Administrator of CMS under 42 CFR § 423.503, agree to the following for the purposes of §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31) of the Social Security Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').

## Article I

## Voluntary Medicare Prescription Drug Plan

- A. PDP Sponsor agrees to operate one or more Medicare Voluntary Prescription Drug Plans (hereinafter referred to as a 'PDP'), as described in its application and related materials submitted to CMS for Medicare approval, including but not limited to all the attestations contained therein, and in compliance with the provisions of this contract, which incorporates in its entirety the 2025 Solicitation for Applications for Medicare Prescription Drug Plan Contracts, released on January 9, 2024 (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'the contract'). PDP Sponsor also agrees to operate in accordance with §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31) of the Act, the regulations at 42 CFR Part 423 (with the exception of Subparts Q, R, and S), and the solicitation, as well as all other applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies outlined in guidance, such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance, Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance, CMS Participant Guides, Health Plan Management System memos, Rate Announcement, and trainings. Except as provided in paragraph (C) of this Article, this contract is deemed to incorporate any changes that are required by statute to be implemented during the term of this contract and any regulations implementing or interpreting such statutory provisions.
- B. CMS agrees to perform its obligations to PDP Sponsor consistent with §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 of the Act (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31), the regulations at 42 CFR Part 423 (with the exception of Subparts Q, R, and S), and the solicitation, as well as all other applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies outlined in guidance, such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance, Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance, CMS Participant Guides, Health Plan Management System memos, Rate Announcement, and trainings.
- C. CMS agrees that it will not implement, other than at the beginning of a calendar year, regulations under 42 CFR Part 423 that impose new, significant regulatory requirements on PDP Sponsor. This provision does not apply to new requirements mandated by statute. [42 CFR § 423.516]
- D. If PDP Sponsor had a contract with CMS for Contract Year 2024 under the contract ID number designated above, this document is considered a renewal of the existing contract. While the terms of this document supersede the terms of the 2024 contract, the parties' execution of this contract does not extinguish or interrupt any pending obligations or actions that may have arisen under the 2024 or prior year contracts.

106|42 CFR § 423.507|42 CFR § 423.507 is a provision within the Code of Federal Regulations that establishes the regulatory framework governing the nonrenewal of contracts between Medicare Part D Prescription Drug Plan (PDP) Sponsors and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). This regulation outlines the specific conditions under which CMS may choose not to renew a PDP Sponsor’s contract, ensuring that such decisions are made in a transparent, timely, and administratively sound manner. A key component of the regulation is the requirement for CMS to provide advance notice of nonrenewal to the PDP Sponsor, with defined timelines that allow the sponsor sufficient time to prepare for the transition. These notice requirements are designed to protect beneficiaries by minimizing disruptions in prescription drug coverage and ensuring continuity of care during the contract transition period.

In addition to notification timelines, 42 CFR § 423.507 includes detailed data transfer obligations for PDP Sponsors upon contract nonrenewal. These obligations mandate that sponsors must securely and completely transfer all beneficiary data, including enrollment information, claims data, and other relevant records, to the successor plan or to CMS as required. This ensures that the continuity of benefits and administrative functions is maintained without loss of critical information. The regulation also emphasizes the importance of data integrity and confidentiality during the transfer process, aligning with broader federal standards for the protection of personal health information.

The provision serves as a critical mechanism for maintaining accountability and operational stability within the Medicare Part D program. By clearly defining the circumstances under which contracts may be nonrenewed and establishing procedural safeguards—such as advance notice and data transfer protocols—42 CFR § 423.507 supports CMS’s ability to manage the PDP marketplace effectively while safeguarding the interests of beneficiaries. It also provides PDP Sponsors with clarity regarding their responsibilities and rights in the event of contract termination, promoting a predictable and fair regulatory environment.

Overall, 42 CFR § 423.507 plays a vital role in the governance of Medicare Part D by balancing CMS’s authority to manage plan participation with the need to ensure beneficiary protection, data security, and administrative continuity. The regulation reflects a comprehensive approach to contract management, integrating procedural fairness, transparency, and operational efficiency into the nonrenewal process.|2

0|## CONTRACT WITH APPROVED ENTITY PURSUANT TO SECTIONS 1860D-1 THROUGH 1860D-43 OF THE SOCIAL SECURITY ACT FOR THE OPERATION OF A VOLUNTARY MEDICARE PRESCRIPTION DRUG PLAN

## CONTRACT (<<CONTRACT\_ID>>)

Between

Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (hereinafter referred to as 'CMS')

And

## <<CONTRACT\_NAME>>

(a Prescription Drug Plan Sponsor, hereinafter referred to as 'PDP Sponsor')

CMS and PDP Sponsor, an entity that has been determined eligible to operate a Voluntary Medicare Prescription Drug Plan by the Administrator of CMS under 42 CFR § 423.503, agree to the following for the purposes of §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31) of the Social Security Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').

## Article I

## Voluntary Medicare Prescription Drug Plan

- A. PDP Sponsor agrees to operate one or more Medicare Voluntary Prescription Drug Plans (hereinafter referred to as a 'PDP'), as described in its application and related materials submitted to CMS for Medicare approval, including but not limited to all the attestations contained therein, and in compliance with the provisions of this contract, which incorporates in its entirety the 2025 Solicitation for Applications for Medicare Prescription Drug Plan Contracts, released on January 9, 2024 (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'the contract'). PDP Sponsor also agrees to operate in accordance with §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31) of the Act, the regulations at 42 CFR Part 423 (with the exception of Subparts Q, R, and S), and the solicitation, as well as all other applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies outlined in guidance, such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance, Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance, CMS Participant Guides, Health Plan Management System memos, Rate Announcement, and trainings. Except as provided in paragraph (C) of this Article, this contract is deemed to incorporate any changes that are required by statute to be implemented during the term of this contract and any regulations implementing or interpreting such statutory provisions.
- B. CMS agrees to perform its obligations to PDP Sponsor consistent with §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 of the Act (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31), the regulations at 42 CFR Part 423 (with the exception of Subparts Q, R, and S), and the solicitation, as well as all other applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies outlined in guidance, such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance, Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance, CMS Participant Guides, Health Plan Management System memos, Rate Announcement, and trainings.
- C. CMS agrees that it will not implement, other than at the beginning of a calendar year, regulations under 42 CFR Part 423 that impose new, significant regulatory requirements on PDP Sponsor. This provision does not apply to new requirements mandated by statute. [42 CFR § 423.516]
- D. If PDP Sponsor had a contract with CMS for Contract Year 2024 under the contract ID number designated above, this document is considered a renewal of the existing contract. While the terms of this document supersede the terms of the 2024 contract, the parties' execution of this contract does not extinguish or interrupt any pending obligations or actions that may have arisen under the 2024 or prior year contracts.
- E. This contract is in no way intended to supersede or modify 42 CFR Part 423. Failure to reference a regulatory requirement in this contract does not affect the applicability of such requirements to PDP Sponsor and CMS.

## A. ENROLLMENT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to accept new enrollments, make enrollments effective, process voluntary disenrollments, and limit involuntary disenrollments, as described in 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart B.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the prohibition in 42 CFR § 423.104(b) on discrimination in beneficiary enrollment.
3. PDP Sponsor shall accept enrollment applications from individuals who change their election during the open enrollment period for individuals enrolled in Medicare Advantage described in 42 CFR § 422.62(a)(3), as required by 42 CFR § 423.38(e).

## B. PRESCRIPTION DRUG BENEFIT

PDP Sponsor agrees to provide the basic prescription drug coverage as defined under 42 CFR § 423.100 and, to the extent applicable, supplemental benefits as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100 and in accordance with Subpart C of 42 CFR Part 423. PDP Sponsor also agrees to provide Part D benefits as described in PDP Sponsor's bid(s) approved each year by CMS (as referenced in the Medicare Advantage Attestation of Benefit Plan, which is included in the contracting materials, and to be replaced each year upon renewal of the contract to reflect PDP Sponsor's approved bids for the succeeding contract year).
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to calculate and collect beneficiary premiums in accordance with 42 CFR §§ 423.286 and 423.293. PDP Sponsor also agrees to

## P. CERTIFICATION OF DATA THAT DETERMINE PAYMENT

PDP Sponsor must provide certifications in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(k).

## Q. ENROLLMENT RELATED COSTS

PDP Sponsor agrees to payment of fees established by CMS for cost sharing of enrollment related costs in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.6.

## R. PDP SPONSOR REIMBURSEMENT TO PHARMACIES [42 CFR §§ 423.505(b)(21) and 423.520]

1. If a PDP Sponsor uses a standard for reimbursement of pharmacies based on the cost of a drug, PDP Sponsor will update such standard not less frequently than once every 7 days, beginning with an initial update on January 1 of each year, to accurately reflect the market price of the drug.
2. If the source for any prescription drug pricing standard is not publicly available, PDP

Sponsor will disclose all individual drug prices to be updated to the applicable pharmacies in advance for their use for the reimbursement of claims.

3. PDP Sponsor will issue, mail, or otherwise transmit payment with respect to all claims submitted by pharmacies (other than pharmacies that dispense drugs by mail order only, or are located in, or contract with, a long-term care facility) within 14 days of receipt of an electronically submitted claim or within 30 days of receipt of a claim submitted otherwise.
4. PDP Sponsor must ensure that a pharmacy located in, or having a contract with, a longterm care facility will have not less than 30 days (but not more than 90 days) to submit claims to PDP Sponsor for reimbursement.

## Article III Record Retention and Reporting Requirements

## A. RECORD MAINTENANCE AND ACCESS

PDP Sponsor agrees to maintain records and provide access in accordance with 42 CFR §§ 423.505(b)(10) and 423.505(i)(2).

## B. GENERAL REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

PDP Sponsor agrees to submit information to CMS according to 42 CFR §§ 423.505(f) and 423.514, and applicable Final Medicare Part D Reporting Guidance.

## C. CMS LICENSE FOR USE OF PLAN FORMULARY

PDP Sponsor agrees to submit to CMS each plan's formulary information, including any changes to its formularies, and hereby grants to the Government, and any person or entity who might receive the formulary from the Government, a non-exclusive license to use all or any portion of the formulary for any purpose related to the administration of the Part D program, including without limitation publicly distributing, displaying, publishing, or reconfiguration of the information in any medium, including www.medicare.gov, and by any electronic, print, or other means of distribution.

## Article IV HIPAA Provisions

- A. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the confidentiality and enrollee record accuracy requirements specified in 42 CFR § 423.136.
- B. PDP Sponsor agrees to enter into a business associate agreement with the entity with which CMS has contracted to track Medicare beneficiaries' true out-of- pocket costs.

Article V

## Requirements of Other Laws and Regulations

PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with (a) applicable Federal laws and regulations designed to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse, including, but not limited to, applicable provisions of Federal criminal law, the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729 et seq.), and the anti-kickback provision of § 1128B of the Act; (b) applicable Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) rules at 45 CFR Parts 160, 162, and 164; and (c) all other applicable Federal statutes and regulations.

## Article VI Contract Term and Renewal

## A. TERM OF CONTRACT

This contract is effective from the date of CMS's authorized representative's signature through December 31, 2025. This contract shall be renewable for successive one-year periods thereafter according to 42 CFR § 423.506.

## B. QUALIFICATION TO RENEW A CONTRACT

1. In accordance with 42 CFR § 423.507, PDP Sponsor will be determined qualified to renew its contract annually only if PDP Sponsor has not provided CMS with a notice of intention not to renew in accordance with Article VII of this contract.
2. Although PDP Sponsor may be determined qualified to renew its contract under this Article, if PDP Sponsor and CMS cannot reach agreement on the bid under Subpart F of 42 CFR Part 423 and CMS declines to accept the bid pursuant to 42 CFR § 423.265(b)(4), no renewal takes place, and, in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.502(d)(2), the failure to reach agreement is not subject to the appeals provisions in Subpart N of 42 CFR Part 423.

## Article VII Nonrenewal of Contract by PDP Sponsor

- D. If PDP Sponsor does not renew a contract, it must ensure the timely transfer of any data or files in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.507(a)(5).

## Article VIII Modification or Termination of Contract

## A. CONTRACT MODIFICATION OR TERMINATION BY MUTUAL CONSENT

1. This contract may be modified or terminated at any time by written mutual consent of the parties. If the PDP Sponsor submits a request to end the term of this contract after the deadline provided in 42 CFR § 423.507(a)(2)(i), CMS may mutually consent to the contract termination if the contract termination does not negatively affect the administration of the Medicare Part D Program.
2. If this contract is terminated by mutual consent, PDP Sponsor must provide notice to its Medicare enrollees and the general public in accordance with CMS's instructions.
3. As set forth in 42 CFR § 423.508, if the contract is modified by mutual consent, PDP Sponsor must notify its Medicare enrollees of any changes that CMS determines are appropriate for notification according to the process and timeframes specified by CMS.
4. If a contract is terminated under this section, PDP Sponsor must ensure the timely transfer of any data or files.
5. If a contract is terminated under this section, CMS cannot enter into a new contract or service area expansion in the PDP region or regions served by the contract with PDP Sponsor or with an organization whose covered persons, as defined in 42 CFR § 423.508(f), also served as covered persons for the terminating PDP Sponsor for a period of up to 2 years unless there are circumstances that warrant special consideration, as determined by CMS. A PDP Sponsor that agrees to terminate its offering of PBPs in a PDP region also agrees that it will not be eligible to apply to resume offering plans in that region for 2 years. [42 CFR § 423.508(e)]

## B. TERMINATION OF CONTRACT BY CMS

CMS may terminate the contract in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.509.

## C. TERMINATION OF CONTRACT BY PDP SPONSOR

PDP Sponsor may terminate the contract only in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.510.

## Article IX Compliance and Enforcement Actions

## A. INTERMEDIATE SANCTIONS

Consistent with Subpart O of 42 CFR Part 423, PDP Sponsor shall be subject to sanctions and civil money penalties.

## B. COMPLIANCE ACTIONS AND PAST PERFORMANCE

CMS may determine that the PDP Sponsor is out of compliance with a Part D requirement and take compliance actions as described in 42 CFR § 423.505(n) or issue intermediate sanctions as defined in 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart O. [42 CFR § 423.505(n)]

## Article X Severability

Severability of the contract shall be in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.504(e).

## Article XI Miscellaneous

## A. DEFINITIONS

Terms not otherwise defined in this contract shall have the meaning given to such terms in §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 of the Act and 42 CFR Part 423.

## B. ALTERATION TO ORIGINAL CONTRACT TERMS

PDP Sponsor agrees and attests that it has not altered in any way the terms of the PDP contract presented for signature by CMS. PDP Sponsor agrees that any alterations to the original text that PDP Sponsor may make to this contract shall not be binding on the parties.

## C. ADDITIONAL CONTRACT TERMS

PDP Sponsor agrees to include in this contract other terms and conditions in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(j).

1. If a PDP Sponsor uses a standard for reimbursement of pharmacies based on the cost of a drug, PDP Sponsor will update such standard not less frequently than once every 7 days, beginning with an initial update on January 1 of each year, to accurately reflect the market price of the drug.

Sponsor will disclose all individual drug prices to be updated to the applicable pharmacies in advance for their use for the reimbursement of claims.

PDP Sponsor agrees to submit to CMS each plan's formulary information, including any changes to its formularies, and hereby grants to the Government, and any person or entity who might receive the formulary from the Government, a non-exclusive license to use all or any portion of the formulary for any purpose related to the administration of the Part D program, including without limitation publicly distributing, displaying, publishing, or reconfiguration of the information in any medium, including www.medicare.gov, and by any electronic, print, or other means of distribution.

PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with (a) applicable Federal laws and regulations designed to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse, including, but not limited to, applicable provisions of Federal criminal law, the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729 et seq.), and the anti-kickback provision of § 1128B of the Act; (b) applicable Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) rules at 45 CFR Parts 160, 162, and 164; and (c) all other applicable Federal statutes and regulations.

6|Medicare Part D Community: CMS, PDP Sponsors, and Beneficiaries|"# Medicare Part D Community: CMS, PDP Sponsors, and Beneficiaries

The Medicare Part D community is a structured network centered on the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), which oversees the federal prescription drug benefit program. Key entities include beneficiaries, PDP Sponsors, and regulatory frameworks, all interconnected through contractual obligations, enrollment processes, benefit delivery, and compliance mechanisms. The community operates under strict federal oversight, with CMS enforcing regulations, managing contract renewals, and ensuring equitable access to prescription drug coverage. Critical components include bid submissions, premium calculations, enrollment periods, and the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan, all designed to maintain affordability and continuity of care for millions of beneficiaries.

## CMS as the central governing authority

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) serves as the central governing entity in the Medicare Part D community, responsible for administering, regulating, and overseeing the entire program. CMS manages contract relationships with PDP Sponsors, enforces compliance with federal regulations, and ensures the delivery of prescription drug benefits to eligible beneficiaries. Its role extends to policy development, data management through the Health Plan Management System, and the implementation of new rules via regulatory updates and training sessions. The agency’s oversight is critical in maintaining program integrity, ensuring financial accountability, and protecting beneficiary rights across all aspects of Part D operations [Data: Entities (43, 15); Relationships (15, 128, 131, 130, 121, +more)].

## Beneficiaries as core recipients of Part D benefits

Beneficiaries are the primary recipients of Medicare Part D benefits, defined as individuals who are eligible for and enrolled in the program, receiving prescription drug coverage through a PDP Sponsor. These individuals are responsible for premium payments, plan selection, and enrollment decisions during the open enrollment period. Their access to benefits is protected by regulations prohibiting discrimination in enrollment, ensuring equal opportunity regardless of health status. Beneficiaries also benefit from financial assistance programs such as the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan (MPPP), which allows installment payments for premiums, reducing upfront financial burdens. The program’s success is measured in part by beneficiary satisfaction, continuity of care, and access to a broad formulary of covered drugs [Data: Entities (26, 43); Relationships (93, 114, 117, 119, 120, +more)].

## PDP Sponsors as key operational partners

PDP Sponsors are private insurance companies or organizations contracted by CMS to deliver Medicare Part D benefits. They are responsible for designing and offering prescription drug plans, submitting bids, collecting premiums, managing enrollment, and ensuring compliance with federal regulations. Sponsors must adhere to strict rules regarding benefit design, cost-sharing, formulary management, and non-discrimination in enrollment. Their contracts are subject to annual renewal, during which prior obligations remain active, ensuring continuity of service. Sponsors also participate in the Part D Redesign Program, which aims to improve plan effectiveness and beneficiary outcomes. Their performance is monitored through CMS data systems, and they are required to submit attestation documents detailing approved benefits and bid information [Data: Entities (43, 29, 28, 34, 23); Relationships (107, 87, 118, 121, 120, +more)].

## Regulatory and compliance framework ensures program integrity

The Medicare Part D community operates under a comprehensive regulatory framework governed by federal statutes and regulations, including 42 CFR § 423.100, § 423.104(b), and § 423.38(e). These rules ensure that PDP Sponsors provide equitable access, maintain accurate billing, and comply with enrollment and disenrollment procedures. The prohibition on discrimination in enrollment (42 CFR § 423.104(b)) is enforced through CMS oversight and compliance checks. Regulatory implementation is facilitated through training sessions, guidance documents, and system updates, ensuring that PDP Sponsors understand and apply new rules correctly. Additionally, statutory changes enacted by Congress may require immediate adjustments to program operations, which must be implemented during the contract term. This robust compliance infrastructure helps maintain trust, transparency, and accountability across the program [Data: Entities (40, 32, 44, 19); Relationships (128, 131, 116, 115, 83, +more)].

## Contractual continuity through renewal and pending obligations

The Medicare Part D program operates on a yearly contract cycle, with PDP Sponsors renewing their agreements with CMS annually. The contract renewal process (e.g., 2024 to 2025) supersedes prior terms but maintains active obligations from previous contracts, ensuring uninterrupted service and compliance. These pending obligations include commitments related to benefit delivery, cost-sharing, and beneficiary protections, which remain enforceable even after a new contract is signed. This continuity is critical for maintaining stability in the program, especially for beneficiaries who rely on consistent access to medications. The renewal process is supported by the Medicare Advantage Attestation of Benefit Plan, which documents approved benefits and bids, and is updated annually to reflect current plan offerings [Data: Entities (37, 38, 23); Relationships (121, 123, 87, 118, 119, +more)].

## Open enrollment and enrollment management processes

The open enrollment period is a critical annual window during which Medicare beneficiaries can enroll in, change, or disenroll from Medicare Part D plans. This period is governed by 42 CFR § 422.62(a)(3) and requires PDP Sponsors to accept enrollment applications from beneficiaries. The process is designed to ensure timely access to coverage and to allow beneficiaries to make informed decisions based on plan performance, premiums, and formulary options. PDP Sponsors must also process voluntary disenrollments in accordance with federal regulations, while involuntary disenrollments are strictly limited and subject to compliance requirements. The Health Plan Management System supports these processes by tracking enrollment data, contract information, and compliance reporting, enabling real-time monitoring and accountability [Data: Entities (25, 31, 33); Relationships (91, 114, 117, 130, 89, +more)].

## Financial mechanisms support beneficiary affordability

Several financial mechanisms are in place to ensure that Medicare Part D remains affordable for beneficiaries. The Medicare Prescription Payment Plan (MPPP) allows enrollees to pay their premiums in installments rather than as a lump sum, improving budgeting and access for those with limited financial resources. Premiums are calculated and collected in accordance with 42 CFR §§ 423.286 and 423.293, ensuring consistency and compliance. Additionally, the Part D Manufacturer Discount Program requires pharmaceutical companies to provide discounts to Part D plans, which reduce beneficiary cost-sharing and lower out-of-pocket expenses. These mechanisms collectively help mitigate the financial burden of prescription drugs, particularly for low-income individuals who may qualify for the Low-Income Subsidy (LIS) [Data: Entities (34, 27, 35); Relationships (118, 119, 106, 120, 121, +more)].

## Part D Redesign Program drives structural improvements

The Part D Redesign Program, initiated by CMS, is a strategic effort to enhance the structure, effectiveness, and sustainability of the Medicare Part D program. This initiative includes changes to benefit design, cost-sharing models, and plan performance metrics, as detailed in the Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions. The program aims to improve beneficiary outcomes, increase transparency, and promote competition among PDP Sponsors. It also supports the integration of new technologies and data analytics to better monitor plan performance and identify areas for improvement. The redesign is implemented through updated regulations and guidance, requiring PDP Sponsors to adapt their plans to meet new standards. This ongoing evolution reflects CMS’s commitment to modernizing the program and ensuring long-term affordability and accessibility [Data: Entities (36); Relationships (120, 121, 128, 131, 118, +more)]."
